chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Basri al-Bazzaz reported to me from Abu Bishr Ahmad ibn Ibrahim, who reported from Zakariyya ibn Yahya al-Saji, who reported from Abdul Jabbar, from Sufyan, from al-Walid ibn Kathir, from Ibn al-Sayyad, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab who said:

When the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, died, the whole Mecca was shaken with deep sorrow. Then Abu Quhafa said: 'What is happening?' They told him: 'The Prophet has departed.' He said: 'Who has assumed authority over people after him?' They told him: 'Your son.' He asked: 'Did Banu Abd Shams and Banu al-Mughira approve?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'No one can prevent that which Allah bestows and no one can give what Allah takes away. What a surprise! They dispute the Prophethood and easily give the Caliphate! Surely, this seems to have been destined.'

key_terms.الخلافة: Caliphate - succession to political leadership after the Prophet
key_terms.النبوة: Prophethood - the divine mission of Muhammad
key_terms.بنو المغيرة: Banu al-Mughira - a powerful Quraysh clan (Banu Makhzum)
key_terms.بنو عبد شمس: Banu Abd Shams - a major Quraysh clan, ancestors of the Umayyads

ai.seo_question: What did Abu Quhafa say about the caliphate after the Prophet Muhammad's death?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the reaction of Abu Quhafa, Abu Bakr's father, upon learning of the Prophet's death and Abu Bakr's assumption of the caliphate. His immediate concern was whether the powerful Quraysh clans (Banu Abd Shams and Banu al-Mughira) had accepted, and his comment about disputing prophethood while conceding the caliphate reflects the political tensions of early Islamic succession.
